title: Hampden P1294
memorial_details: IWM records a black wooden board with gilt lettering, about 450mm square, fixed 4 metres up a tree trunk beside the A495 at Llynclys, in good condition. Its inscription honours those who fought to land the burning, damaged bomber without injury to others, that the tree added another obstacle to the fatal crash in the field opposite, and that all crew were killed. IWM does not transcribe whatever follows 'IN HONOUR OF'. IBCC transcribes the board as 'In honour of the crew of Hampden P1294' and calls it stencilled. IBCC also lists a tablet for Cottesmore station personnel in the Church of St. Nicholas, Cottesmore. IWM does not state who made or erected the board, when, or who looks after it.
inscription: IN HONOUR OF/ WHO BRAVELY FOUGHT TO LAND BURNING &/ BADLY DAMAGED HAMPDEN BOMBER No P1294/ WITHOUT INJURY TO OTHERS./ THIS TREE ADDING ANOTHER OBSTACLE TO/ THE FATAL CRASH IN FIELD OPPOSITE/ KILLING ALL CREW./ OCTOBER 30TH 1941

sources.title: 14 Operational Training Unit Hampden I P1294 F/O. Kerr, RAF Cottesmore, Training

narrative:
Hampden I P1294 of 14 Operational Training Unit took off from RAF Cottesmore on a cross-country navigation flight and crashed at about 14:30 on 30 October 1941 in a field at White Lion crossroads on Llynclys Hill, near Oswestry. Aircrew Remembered says the aircraft had just cleared the Berwyn mountains in very poor visibility and driving rain, and that the pilot had just been given a corrected course back to Cottesmore. IBCC records it as seen to emerge almost vertically from cloud. Aircrew Remembered adds that witnesses saw it clip trees and a high-tension wire before it crashed, caught fire and exploded; other reports say it had levelled out, as if trying to land. All four crew died. We found no formal inquiry finding.

The pilot was Flying Officer George Donald Kerr (26), son of Richard and Isabella Kerr and husband of Phyllis, buried at Liverpool (Allerton) Cemetery. The observer was Sergeant Ivor Morgan Williams (19) of Newport, buried at Cardiff (Cathays) Cemetery; his brother also died on service. The two wireless operator/air gunners were Sergeant Douglas Tatton (21) of Erdington, Birmingham, buried at Erdington (St Barnabas) Churchyard, and Sergeant Herbert Playforth (21) of York, buried at Brompton Cemetery, Northallerton. Tatton had lost his brother Cyril on a Brest raid three months earlier. All four served in the RAFVR. Tatton's details rest on Aircrew Remembered alone.

crew.name: Herbert Playforth
crew.burial_location: Brompton Cemetery, Northallerton, Sec. C, Grave 111

external_narratives.summary: IWM entry for the wooden plaque on a tree at Llynclys. The inscription has a '(Names)' placeholder after 'IN HONOUR OF', so no person is named. Maker, dedication date, erector and custodian are not stated. No IWM capture existed in research/iwm/ for this memorial, so the live page was read.
